title: Peshwa Bajirao II
subtitle: Subsidiary alliance and the fall of the Peshwa state · 1796 – 1818
subject: bajirao-ii
intro: The last Peshwa came to power in 1796 amid feuding between the great Maratha houses. Driven out of Pune by Yashwantrao Holkar in 1802, he accepted British protection in the Treaty of Bassein — which led to two wars with the East India Company and, in 1818, the end of the Peshwa state and of Maratha independence.

events.title: Sawai Madhavrao dies
events.summary: The young Peshwa's death opens the way for Raghunathrao's son, kept under guard at Shivneri and Junnar.

events.title: Nana Phadnavis arrested
events.summary: Bajirao and Daulatrao Shinde have Nana seized and held at Ahmednagar fort; he is released the next year.

events.title: Trimbakji escapes from Thane
events.summary: Bajirao's favourite Trimbakji Dengle, handed over to the British over the Gangadhar Shastri murder, escapes from Thane jail and raises troops.

events.title: Settled at Bithur
events.summary: On a British pension of eight lakhs a year, Bajirao is sent to live at Bithur near Kanpur.

events.title: Nana Sahib adopted
events.summary: Bajirao adopts Dhondu Pant, later famous as Nana Sahib of 1857.

events.title: Bajirao born
events.summary: Bajirao is born at Dhar to Raghunathrao and Anandibai while his father is at war with Nana Phadnavis's government.

events.title: Grows up under guard
events.summary: After his father's death Bajirao and his brothers are kept under watch by Nana Phadnavis's government, mostly at Junnar and Shivneri.

events.title: Becomes Peshwa
events.summary: After Sawai Madhavrao's death and months of manoeuvring between Nana Phadnavis and Daulatrao Shinde, Bajirao II is installed as Peshwa.

events.title: Nana Phadnavis dies
events.summary: With Nana's death Pune becomes the battleground of rival chiefs, chiefly Daulatrao Shinde and Yashwantrao Holkar.

events.title: Execution of Vithoji Holkar
events.summary: Bajirao has Yashwantrao Holkar's brother Vithoji trampled by an elephant. Yashwantrao vows revenge.

events.title: Battle of Poona — Bajirao flees
events.summary: Yashwantrao Holkar defeats the combined armies of the Peshwa and Shinde at Hadapsar outside Pune. Bajirao flees to the coast and takes refuge with the British.

events.title: Treaty of Bassein
events.summary: At Vasai (Bassein), Bajirao signs a subsidiary alliance: a British force will be stationed in his territory at his cost, and he gives up an independent foreign policy. The other Maratha chiefs see it as a surrender of Maratha independence.

events.title: Restored in Pune by British troops
events.summary: Arthur Wellesley's army escorts Bajirao back to Pune and reinstates him as Peshwa.

events.title: Battle of Assaye — Second Anglo-Maratha War
events.summary: Shinde and the Bhonsle of Nagpur fight the British over Bassein. Wellesley defeats their army at Assaye in a costly battle he later called the bloodiest he ever saw.

events.title: Delhi and Laswari
events.summary: In the north, Gerard Lake defeats Shinde's forces at Delhi (September) and Laswari (November). The Mughal emperor passes under British protection.

events.title: Shinde and Bhonsle accept defeat
events.summary: By the treaties of Deogaon and Surji-Anjangaon, the Bhonsle of Nagpur and Daulatrao Shinde cede large territories, including Delhi and Agra, to the Company.

events.title: Holkar's war and the siege of Bharatpur
events.summary: Yashwantrao Holkar fights on. The British fail to take the Jat fortress of Bharatpur, where he had sheltered, after four assaults. He makes peace at the end of 1805 on relatively favourable terms.

events.title: Yashwantrao Holkar dies
events.summary: The last major Maratha chief to fight the British on his own terms dies at Bhanpura.

events.title: Murder of Gangadhar Shastri
events.summary: The Gaekwad's envoy Gangadhar Shastri is murdered at Pandharpur while under the Peshwa's safe conduct. The British resident Elphinstone blames the Peshwa's favourite Trimbakji Dengle and forces his surrender.

events.title: Treaty of Poona
events.summary: Under pressure, Bajirao signs away territory and formally renounces his position as head of the Maratha confederacy.

events.title: Battle of Khadki — the last war begins
events.summary: Bajirao attacks the British at Khadki, outside Pune, and is defeated. The Third Anglo-Maratha War begins; on 17 November the British occupy Pune and raise their flag over Shaniwar Wada.

events.title: Battle of Sitabuldi
events.summary: Appasaheb Bhonsle of Nagpur turns on the British resident and is defeated at Sitabuldi hill.

events.title: Battle of Mahidpur
events.summary: The Holkar army is defeated at Mahidpur. The Holkar state survives as a British-protected princely state.

events.title: Battle of Koregaon
events.summary: A small Company force, largely Mahar soldiers of the Bombay Native Infantry, holds Koregaon village for a day against a much larger part of the Peshwa's army. The battle is commemorated today by the Ambedkarite movement as a symbol of resistance to caste oppression.

events.title: Battle of Ashti
events.summary: Bapu Gokhale, the Peshwa's most loyal general, is killed at Ashti. The British free the young Chhatrapati Pratapsinh, who had been travelling with the Peshwa's camp.

events.title: Satara restored under British protection
events.summary: Elphinstone proclaims the end of Peshwa rule and sets up Pratapsinh as ruler of a small Satara state under British supervision.

events.title: Bajirao surrenders — the end of the Peshwa state
events.summary: Bajirao surrenders to Sir John Malcolm in Malwa in return for a large pension and exile at Bithur near Kanpur. The Peshwa's territories are annexed by the East India Company.

events.title: Dies in exile at Bithur
events.summary: Bajirao dies at Bithur. The Company refuses to continue his pension to his adopted son Nana Sahib — a grievance that helps make Nana Sahib a leader of the revolt of 1857.
